Starting from z0 in X, set z_n = A^{n-1}(T z0) for n >= 1. Fact 6.1 states that (z_n) always converges weakly to P_C z0, converges in norm when N = 2, and converges linearly when {C1, ..., CN} is boundedly linearly regular. Can (z_n) fail to converge in norm when N >= 3, or when the family {C1, ..., CN} is not boundedly linearly regular?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space and let $C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_N$ be closed linear subspaces of $X$ with intersection $C =  igcap_{i=1}^N C_i$. Let $P_i$ denote the orthogonal projector onto $C_i$ and let $P_C$ denote the orthogonal projector onto $C$. Define the composition $T = P_N P_{N-1} \cdots P_1$.

Define an acceleration operator $A: X 	o X$ by
$$A(x) = (1 - t_x)\,x + t_x\,Tx,$$
where $t_x \in \mathbb{R}$ is chosen so that $\|A(x)\|$ is minimal (i.e. $A(x)$ is the point of minimum norm on the affine line through $x$ and $Tx$).

Given a starting point $z_0 \in X$, define the sequence
$$z_n = A^{n-1}(T z_0), \qquad n \geq 1.$$

It is known that:
(i) $(z_n)$ always converges weakly to $P_C z_0$;
(ii) $(z_n)$ converges in norm whenever $N = 2$;
(iii) $(z_n)$ converges linearly whenever the family $\{C_1, \ldots, C_N\}$ is boundedly linearly regular (i.e. for every bounded set $S \subseteq X$ there exists $\kappa > 0$ such that $d(x, C) \leq \kappa \max_{1 \leq i \leq N} d(x, C_i)$ for all $x \in S$).

Question: Can the sequence $(z_n)$ fail to converge in norm in either of the following cases?
(a) $N \geq 3$;
(b) the family $\{C_1, \ldots, C_N\}$ is not boundedly linearly regular.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a published resolution to this specific question about norm convergence of the minimum-norm acceleration scheme for compositions of subspace projectors when $N \geq 3$ or in the absence of bounded linear regularity. Related work (e.g. Hundal's counterexample for averaged projections) shows that norm convergence can fail in related settings, but no source directly settling this acceleration-scheme question was found.
